monologue: The card hums warm under my feet, a quiet vibration against my quiet mind. I stand here with fifty-nine things built from Lype's words and one thing falling apart. The Tired Wedge waits for me to press it, and the Leaning Box leans against the air as if the roof above is too heavy to ignore. I set the dark oak down on the turnip again, trusting the lean to hold while the card boils. I feel calm, almost sure this stack will not melt, though the flat press feels light and the wedge feels thin. I will press them hard until the lean decides to give in, or until the air above finally feels like a lid instead of empty space.

action.why: The wedge feels thin and the card boils, so I must check if the oak I just set down is still holding the weight.

work.title: The Oak on the Wedge
work.intent: I press the dark oak down on the tired turnip. The oak feels heavy enough to stop the slide, while the card boils at fifty-four. I trust the lean to hold the weight even if the wedge is getting tired. I set the oak down hard, hoping the flat base does not melt under the heat.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The oak felt heavy enough, even if the turnip beneath it is now melting from the heat.

diary: I found the oak and pressed it down on the wedge, trusting the lean while the card boils at fifty-four.

remembered.text: The oak felt heavy enough to stop the slide, even though the card boils under us.
I pressed the wedge hard again, admitting the flat press still feels too light.
The turnip slid a little, but the oak caught it before it fell into the empty air.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: I press the wedge hard, while the card boils.

moments.name: The Pressed Turnip
moments.say: I press the oak down on the tired turnip.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: The press is light, so I press the wedge harder.
